source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 1. Bios Setting EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> Lock Chipset -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> Processor Configuration -> MSR Lock Control -> Disabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> EV DFX features -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Socket Configuration -> IIO Configuration -> IIO DFX Configuration -> Disable BIOS Done -> [‘X’] EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> WHEA Error Injection Support -> Enabled EDKII Menu -> Platform Configuration -> System Event Log -> Error Injection Settings -> Whea PCIE Error Injection Action Table -> Enabled 2. Deploy Intel ITP environment. 3. Boot SUT into Windows. 4. Execute Intel Cscripts on the client 5. Using the following command >>>itp.log("C:\Test.log") >>>halt() >>>pcie.topology() >>>ei.pcie_port_map__pch() 6. Check PCIe PCH target >>>ei.injectPcieError_pch(port, errType='uce') >>>go 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- Uncorrectable Error (Intel PCH Uncorrectable Error error injection): requires CScripts/EDKII unlock (Lock Chipset=Disable, MSR Lock Control=Disable, EV DFX Features=Enable, WHEA Error Injection Support=Enable) + the user/FAE to drive the Cscript/error-injection harness for this exact pattern.
